pieces.body:
Modeled on AIA Document A133-2009, with Owner modifications. Guaranteed Maximum Price.

> SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT. This is a fictional contract written for INFO 492 C coursework. It is modeled on a publicly documented school GC/CM project, but it is not that project's actual contract.

Project: School Modernization and Addition (the "Project")
Owner: Example School District No. 1 ("Owner")
Construction Manager: Example Builders, Inc. ("CM")
Architect: Example Architecture, PLLC ("Architect")
Effective Date: June 17, 2019
Guaranteed Maximum Price: $26,240,507

Contract Documents. The Contract Documents are this Agreement, Exhibits A through E, the Drawings and Specifications (including Division 01, excerpted in Exhibit E), Addenda, and Modifications issued after the Effective Date.

Order of Precedence. If the Contract Documents conflict, they control in this order: (a) executed Modifications; (b) Articles 1 through 14; (c) Exhibits A through D; (d) Exhibit E; (e) Drawings and other Specifications. Exhibit E may add procedural detail, but it does not shorten any notice period or lengthen any response time stated in the Articles.

Definitions.

- Change Order (CO): a written instrument signed by Owner, Architect, and CM that adjusts the GMP, the Contract Time, or both.
- Change Proposal (CP): CM's priced request for an adjustment to the GMP or Contract Time.
- Construction Change Directive (CCD): a written order signed by Owner directing a change before the adjustment is agreed.
- Architect's Supplemental Instruction (ASI): a written instruction by Architect that is not intended to change cost or time.
- RFI: a written request from CM to Architect for clarification of the Contract Documents.
- Potential Change: any RFI response, ASI, direction, condition, or event that CM believes will increase cost or time.
- Specified General Conditions (SGC): the fixed-price field management and site costs listed in Exhibit C.
- Negotiated Support Services (NSS): the support services listed in Exhibit C and priced as lump sums.
- Self-Performed Work (SPW): Work performed by CM's own forces.
Time Periods. "Days" means calendar days unless stated otherwise. If a period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, it ends on the next business day.
Services. CM shall provide construction management and general contracting services for the Project as a GC/CM and shall furnish all labor, materials, and equipment needed to complete the Work.

Review of Documents. CM shall carefully study the Contract Documents and shall promptly report to Architect, as an RFI, any error, inconsistency, or omission it discovers. CM is not responsible for errors in the Contract Documents unless it knowingly failed to report them.

No Authority to Change Scope. CM shall not perform changed Work, and no RFI response, ASI, meeting minute, or oral direction authorizes added cost or time, until a CO or CCD is issued. Work on a change without a CO or CCD is at CM's risk.
Commencement. CM shall begin the Work on the date stated in the Notice to Proceed, issued by Owner.
Substantial Completion. CM shall achieve Substantial Completion within 540 days after the Notice to Proceed, and Final Completion within 60 days after Substantial Completion.
Liquidated Damages. If CM fails to achieve Substantial Completion on time, CM shall pay Owner $2,500 for each day of delay.

Time Extensions. Contract Time is extended only by CO. An extension is available only for delays outside CM's control that are shown on the critical path, and only if CM has given notice under Section 6.2.

GMP. The Guaranteed Maximum Price is $26,240,507. It covers the Cost of the Work, CM's Fee, SGC, NSS, and CM Contingency, itemized in Exhibit A. CM shall pay any cost that would cause the GMP to be exceeded, unless a CO has adjusted the GMP.
Savings. Any savings in the GMP belong to Owner.

CM Contingency. The CM Contingency is $338,007. CM may use it only for costs within CM's reasonable control, such as subcontract buyout variances and CM's own coordination errors, and only with Owner's written approval before the cost is incurred. The CM Contingency may not be used for Owner-requested changes or for RFI or ASI changes, which are handled under Article 6.
Adjustments. The GMP is adjusted only by CO.
CM's Fee. CM's Fee is 5% of the sum of the Subcontract Work and SPW shown in Exhibit A, which is $1,122,500. The Fee is fixed and changes only as stated in Article 6.

Specified General Conditions. SGC is $1,720,000, billed as shown in Exhibit C. SGC may be increased only by CO for an extension of Contract Time, at a daily rate of $3,185 per day. No Fee is added to SGC.
Negotiated Support Services. NSS is $610,000, billed as shown in Exhibit C. No Fee is added to NSS, and NSS changes only by CO.

Reimbursable Costs. Reimbursable Cost of the Work includes subcontract payments, materials, CM labor at the rates in the approved labor schedule plus a fixed labor burden of 32% of direct wages, bond and insurance premiums at actual cost, Washington B&O taxes at actual cost, and permit fees.

Costs Covered by the Fee or SGC. The following are covered by the Fee or SGC and shall not be billed separately, including on a CP: home office overhead; estimating, accounting, and purchasing; salaries of CM's executives; the supervisory and management positions listed in Exhibit C; field office and project vehicles; hand tools and small tools under $1,000 per item; and the cost of preparing, pricing, and negotiating Change Proposals.

Self-Performed Work. SPW shall not exceed 30% of the Subcontract Work and SPW combined (excluding SGC and NSS) over the life of the Project. CM may self-perform only trades for which its sealed bid was the lowest responsive bid. CM shall report the running SPW percentage with each Application for Payment.

Subcontracting. CM shall competitively bid all Subcontract Work. CM shall give Owner at least 10 days' written notice before awarding any subcontract to a firm related to CM through ownership, management, or family ties.
Types of Change. Changes are made by Change Order, Construction Change Directive, or Architect's Supplemental Instruction.

Review of Change Proposals. Owner, through Architect, shall respond to a complete CP within 14 days after receipt. An incomplete CP shall be returned within 7 days with the missing items identified. Silence is not acceptance. If Owner has not responded after 14 days, CM may send a written reminder and treat the lack of response as a basis for a claim under Article 10.
Pricing Rules.
Direct costs. Direct costs are labor with the fixed burden in Section 5.4, materials at actual cost net of discounts, equipment under Section 6.5.4, and subcontract costs.

Subcontractor markup. A subcontractor may add overhead and profit of up to 10% on its own direct cost and up to 5% on the cost of work performed by its lower-tier subcontractors. Total markup on any portion of the work shall not exceed 15%.

CM's Fee on changes. CM may add a Fee of 5% to the direct costs and subcontractor markups of a change. No Fee is added to NSS, SGC adjustments, bond and insurance premiums, B&O taxes, or permit fees. On deductive changes, the Fee is reduced at the same 5% rate.

Equipment. Equipment listed as included in SGC in Exhibit B shall not be charged to a CP. Other CM-owned equipment is charged at 75% of the current published Blue Book rental rate, and rented equipment at the invoiced cost with no markup other than the Fee. Equipment is charged only for the hours it is actually used on the changed Work, supported by daily logs. Idle equipment is charged at 50% of the applicable rate and only when the idle time is caused by the change.
Costs not chargeable. The items in Section 5.5 shall not be included in a CP.

Time impacts. A time extension is compensated only for delays caused by Owner or Architect that are on the critical path, using the SGC daily rate in Section 5.2 and with no Fee. Delays with concurrent causes receive time but no compensation.

Time-and-material work. T&M tags shall be submitted within 3 business days after the work is performed and signed by CM's superintendent and Owner's Representative. Unsigned tags are not accepted as backup.

Construction Change Directives. Owner may issue a CCD directing CM to proceed with a change before the price is agreed. CM shall proceed. CM shall submit its CP within 14 days after receiving the CCD. If the parties have not agreed within 30 days after the CP is submitted, the cost is determined as the actual Cost of the Work calculated under Section 6.5, plus the Fee, and CM may pursue any disagreement as a claim. Within 45 days after the price is agreed, the CCD shall be converted to a CO.

Approval of Change Orders. A CO is effective only when signed by Owner, Architect, and CM. Owner's Representative may approve a CO of up to $250,000. A CO above $250,000, or a series of related changes totaling more than $250,000, requires approval by Owner's Board of Directors, and CM shall allow time for the Board's schedule when planning the change.

Supplemental Instructions. Architect may issue ASIs that do not change cost or time. If CM believes an ASI will change cost or time, it shall give notice under Section 6.2(a) before proceeding. Proceeding with an ASI does not waive CM's right to notice, if notice is timely.

Change Log. CM shall keep a log of all CPs, numbered in sequence, showing for each the date of notice, date submitted, amount, status, and the originating RFI, ASI, or CCD. CM shall update the log weekly and submit it with each Application for Payment.

Submitting RFIs. CM shall submit RFIs on the form in Exhibit E. Each RFI shall identify the drawing sheets and specification sections involved, state the question, propose CM's recommended answer, and give the date by which a response is needed.

Review Before Submission. CM shall review the Contract Documents before submitting an RFI. If Architect determines that an RFI was answered in the Contract Documents, Architect may return it without a full response. Architect's review costs for each such RFI beyond the tenth shall be charged to CM at $350 per RFI by deduction from the next Application for Payment.

Response Time. Architect shall respond to each RFI within 10 days after receipt. An RFI marked Critical Path shall be answered within 3 business days. If Architect cannot respond in time, it shall notify CM within 5 days and give the date a response will be provided.
Effect of Responses. An RFI response does not change the Contract Sum or Contract Time. If CM believes a response changes cost or time, CM shall follow Sections 6.2 and 6.3.
Distribution. CM shall send each RFI response to every affected subcontractor within 2 business days. CM shall keep an RFI log, updated weekly, showing the date each RFI was sent and answered.
Unanswered RFIs. If an RFI is unanswered after 10 days, CM may send a written follow-up. If it is unanswered after 15 days, CM may give notice of a Potential Change under Section 6.2(d).

Meeting Minutes. Minutes of coordination meetings are for record only. A statement in meeting minutes is not notice under Section 6.2 and does not authorize a change unless it is repeated in a written notice, CO, or CCD.
Submittal Schedule. CM shall submit a submittal schedule within 30 days after the Notice to Proceed, identifying long-lead items.

Review Times. Architect shall review each submittal within 14 days after receipt and each resubmittal within 10 days. CM shall review and stamp each submittal for compliance and coordination before sending it to Architect.

Approved as Noted. When a submittal is returned as "Approved as Noted" or "Revise and Resubmit," CM shall tell every affected subcontractor within 3 business days. If CM believes a comment changes cost or time, CM shall give notice under Section 6.2(a).
Applications. CM shall submit an Application for Payment by the 25th of each month for Work completed through that date, with the change log, the SPW percentage, and lien waivers.
Payment. Owner shall pay the approved amount within 30 days after receiving a complete Application. Overdue undisputed amounts bear interest at 1% per month.
Retainage. Owner shall retain 5% of each progress payment as required by Washington law.
Changes. CM may bill a change only after a CO is executed or a CCD is issued. CCD work may be billed as costs are incurred, subject to adjustment when the price is agreed.
Final Payment. Final payment is due after Final Completion, receipt of all closeout documents, and the lapse of statutory lien periods.

Claim Notice. A claim for added cost or time shall be made in writing within 21 days after the event giving rise to it, or within 14 days after CM receives Owner's response to a CP that CM disputes, whichever applies. A claim not made in time is waived.
Decision. Owner shall respond to a claim within 30 days after receiving it.
Mediation and Litigation. Unresolved claims shall go to mediation, and then to the Superior Court of King County, Washington. CM shall continue the Work during any dispute.
Records. CM shall keep all cost records for at least 6 years after final payment.

Audit. Owner or its auditor may audit CM's records at any time during that period. Any charge found not allowable under Articles 5 and 6 shall be credited to Owner within 30 days after the audit report, and Owner may offset the amount against money owed to CM.

CM shall furnish payment and performance bonds each for 100% of the GMP, and commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 in the aggregate, naming Owner as additional insured.
For Cause. Owner may terminate for cause if CM fails to cure a material default within 7 days after written notice.
For Convenience. Owner may terminate for convenience on 14 days' written notice and shall pay CM for Work performed and reasonable demobilization costs.
Governing Law. Washington law governs this Agreement.

Notices. Notices shall be in writing and sent to the representatives in Exhibit D. A notice sent through the project management platform designated by Owner is a written notice and is received on the next business day.
No Waiver. Owner's payment or failure to object does not waive any right under this Agreement.

Division 01 Excerpts

Section 01 26 00. Contract Modification Procedures.

1. Proposal Requests. Architect may issue a written Proposal Request describing a possible change. CM shall return a CP within 14 days after receiving it, or within that time explain why more time is needed.
2. CP numbering. CPs are numbered in sequence (CP-0001, CP-0002, and so on). A revised CP keeps its number with a letter suffix.
3. Backup. Every CP shall attach the RFI, ASI, or CCD that caused it, subcontractor quotes with their own breakdowns, equipment logs, and T&M tags.
4. Pay application link. The CP log is submitted with each Application for Payment, as required by Section 6.9.

Section 01 31 00. Project Management and Coordination.

1. RFI form. Each RFI has a unique number, date, sheet and spec references, the question, CM's proposed answer, and the needed-by date.
2. Critical Path RFIs. RFIs marked Critical Path shall state the activity affected and the date the activity will be delayed if no answer is received.
3. Coordination meetings. CM shall hold weekly coordination meetings with the Architect and Owner's Representative and issue minutes within 2 business days. Minutes are not notices, consistent with Section 7.7.

Section 01 33 00. Submittal Procedures.

1. Submittal numbering. Each submittal uses its specification section number and a sequence number.
2. Long-lead items. Items with a lead time over 12 weeks shall be flagged on the submittal schedule and submitted within 45 days after the Notice to Proceed.
3. Stamps. CM shall stamp each submittal before sending it to Architect, confirming it has been checked for compliance and coordination.

Summary. This Section states the procedures for Proposal Requests, Change Proposals (CPs), Construction Change Directives, and Change Orders. Article 6 of the Agreement controls if this Section conflicts with it.

Proposal Requests. Architect may issue a written Proposal Request describing a possible change. CM shall return a CP within 14 days after receiving it, or within that time explain in writing why more time is needed.

Change Proposal content. Each CP shall reference the RFI, ASI, direction, or CCD that caused it and the date of CM's notice, and shall include a breakdown of labor hours and rates, materials, equipment, subcontractor pricing, markup, and Fee, and any claimed time impact in days.
CP numbering. CPs are numbered in sequence (CP-0001, CP-0002, and so on). A revised CP keeps its number with a letter suffix (CP-0201A).

Backup. Every CP shall attach the RFI, ASI, or CCD that caused it, subcontractor quotes with their own line-item breakdowns, equipment logs, and T&M tags. A lump-sum subcontractor quote without a breakdown is not acceptable backup.

Time-and-material tags. T&M tags shall list workers, hours, equipment, and materials for each day, and shall be signed by CM's superintendent and Owner's Representative and submitted within 3 business days after the work is performed. Tags signed only by a subcontractor's foreman are not accepted.
CP log. CM shall keep the CP log required by Section 6.9 of the Agreement and submit it with each Application for Payment.
Summary. Removal and disposal of asbestos-containing materials (ACM) identified in Owner's hazardous materials survey, in the existing building areas shown on the abatement drawings.

Hazardous materials survey. Owner's survey identifies ACM in Wing A floor tile, pipe insulation in Wing B, and gym roofing mastic. The survey did not identify mastic under flooring in classrooms 110 to 116. Quantities in the survey are for information; CM shall verify before abatement.

Suspect materials not in the survey. If CM or the abatement contractor finds suspect material not identified in the survey, stop work in the area, isolate it, sample it, and notify Owner and Architect the same day. Notice of a differing condition is governed by Section 6.2(c) of the Agreement.

Waste handling and disposal. The abatement contractor shall package ACM waste in labeled, sealed containers, transport it in an enclosed vehicle, and dispose of it at a licensed landfill. Waste manifests shall be submitted to Owner within 10 days of disposal.
Restoration. Patching and painting of surfaces disturbed by abatement are not part of this Section; restoration is by the trade sections only where shown on the Drawings.

documents.title: Section 07 62 00 Sheet Metal Flashing and Trim

pieces.body: Summary. Parapet copings, counterflashings, through-wall flashings, and storefront and window head flashings.
Material. Prefinished galvanized steel sheet, ASTM A653, G90 coating, with a two-coat fluoropolymer finish in the color selected by Architect.
Copings. Form parapet copings from 24-gauge sheet with continuous cleats and concealed splice plates at joints.
Counterflashings. Form counterflashings from 24-gauge sheet, set in reglets or surface-mounted with termination bar and sealant.
Installation. Install flashing to SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual details, with expansion joints at 10 feet on center maximum and lapped, sealed joints.
Head flashings. Provide head flashings with end dams and drip edges at every storefront and window opening, turned up behind the weather barrier at least 4 inches.
Summary. Hardware for swinging doors, including hinges, locksets, exit devices, closers, stops, and seals, scheduled in hardware sets HW-1 through HW-9.
Finish. Satin chrome, BHMA 626 (US26D), unless noted otherwise in the hardware sets.
Hardware set HW-1 (classroom doors). Three butt hinges, classroom-function lockset, wall stop, and silencers.
Hardware set HW-2 (corridor doors C101 to C108). Three butt hinges, passage latchset, overhead stop, and silencers. Standard, non-rated hardware.
Hardware set HW-4 (corridor doors C201 to C212). Three butt hinges, passage latchset, surface closer with parallel arm, kick plate, and gasketing.
Installation. Mount hardware at the heights in the DHI recommended locations. Adjust closers for opening force and closing speed to meet accessibility requirements.
Submittals. Product data for studs and track, and a stud schedule showing gauge, spacing, and height for each partition type, with the manufacturer's limiting-height tables.
Studs and track. ASTM C645 steel studs and track, G40 coating, 3-5/8 inch and 6 inch depths as shown.
Gauge. 20-gauge (30 mil) studs are permitted for interior partitions up to 14 feet in height.
Partitions over 14 feet. Gauge and spacing as indicated on the Drawings, at a deflection limit of L/240 under a 5 psf lateral load.
Installation. Install studs at 16 inches on center unless shown otherwise, with deflection track at the top of partitions that run to structure.
Summary. Primary roof drains, overflow roof drains, and their leaders to the building storm drain or to daylight.
Primary roof drains. Cast iron body with flashing clamp, underdeck clamp, and cast iron dome, sized as shown on the plumbing drawings.
Overflow roof drains. Provide where indicated on the Drawings, with a 2-inch water dam above the roof surface. Where none are indicated, none are required.
Leaders. Service-weight cast iron no-hub pipe and fittings, 4-inch minimum, insulated where above occupied spaces.
Installation. Set drains level at the low points of the roof, coordinated with the roofing installer, and test leaders to 10 feet of head for 15 minutes.
Cleanouts. Provide a cleanout at the base of each vertical leader and at each change of direction greater than 45 degrees.
Drawing E-001 does not show where temporary construction power is to be taken from. Please confirm the point of connection for the site office and trailers.
Take temporary power from the existing service at the Wing B electrical room, panel MDP-B, through a new 200 A fused disconnect.

Answered in the Contract Documents. See Drawing E-001 general note 6: temporary power is from the existing service at the Wing B electrical room. CM's proposed connection is acceptable. Returned under Section 7.2.

documents.title: RFI-109 Corridor door fire ratings C101 to C108

pieces.body: Life-safety plan G-002 shows a 1-hour rated corridor at C101 to C108, but the door schedule and hardware set HW-2 show non-rated doors and hardware. Please confirm the required rating.
Provide 90-minute labeled door assemblies with fire-rated hardware in place of HW-2.
Corridor doors C101 to C108 shall be 90-minute assemblies with fire-rated hardware. See ASI-014.

Drawing P-201 shows four primary roof drains at the gym roof and no overflow drains. The gym roof has parapets on all four sides, and the plumbing code requires secondary drainage. Please confirm whether overflow drains are required.
Add two overflow roof drains next to primary drains RD-2 and RD-4, with 4-inch cast iron leaders discharging to daylight at the north wall.
Provide two overflow roof drains as suggested, with 4-inch cast iron leaders to daylight at the north wall. See ASI-007 for revised Drawing P-201 and Section 22 14 26 paragraph 2.02.A.

documents.title: RFI-118 Finish floor elevation at addition connector

pieces.body: The finish floor elevation of the addition is not dimensioned where it meets the existing Wing A corridor. Survey shows the existing corridor at 100'-1 1/4". Please confirm the addition elevation.
Set the addition finish floor at 100'-1 1/4" to match the existing corridor, with no transition strip.
Match the existing corridor elevation of 100'-1 1/4". No transition strip is required. No change to cost or time is intended.

documents.title: RFI-124 Coping gauge at gym parapet

pieces.body: Section 07 62 00 paragraph 2.02.A calls for 24-gauge copings, but detail 3/A-520 at the gym parapet shows a 20-inch-wide coping. 24-gauge will oil-can at that width. Please confirm the gauge.
Use 22-gauge copings at parapets wider than 16 inches.
Accepted. Use 22-gauge copings where the coping is wider than 16 inches. See ASI-019.

Reflected ceiling plan A-501 shows hard-lid gypsum ceilings in the existing corridors with no access panels. Valves, fire dampers, and VAV boxes above these ceilings need access. Please provide access panel locations.
Provide 14 flush 24 x 24 inch access panels at the locations marked on attached sketch SK-131.
Provide 14 flush, gypsum-board-faced access panels, 24 x 24 inches, at the locations on SK-131. Use fire-rated panels where the ceiling is part of a rated assembly.

documents.title: RFI-137 Paint color for exposed structure in commons

pieces.body: The finish schedule on A-700 lists exposed structure in the commons but gives no color. Please confirm the color.
Paint exposed structure P-3 to match the ceiling.
Refer to the finish schedule on A-700, note 12: exposed structure is P-3. Answered in the Contract Documents.

Drawing P-301 shows two floor drains in the kitchen. Food service plan Q-101 shows a dish machine, a tilting kettle, and a walk-in cooler condensate line that each need an indirect drain. Please confirm the number and location of floor drains.
Add three floor drains, at the dish machine, the tilting kettle, and the walk-in cooler.
Provide three added floor drains at the dish machine, the tilting kettle, and the walk-in cooler, as suggested, connected to the grease waste line.

documents.title: RFI-146 Library ceiling height and duct clearance

pieces.body: In the Wing B library the existing beams leave 11 inches below the structure at the perimeter, and the supply duct shown on M-202 is 14 inches deep. Please advise.
Lower the ceiling 4 inches at the library perimeter soffit.
Lower the perimeter soffit 4 inches as suggested. The center ceiling stays at the height shown. No change to cost or time is intended.

documents.title: RFI-152 Stair nosings at existing stairs

pieces.body: Section 09 65 13 calls for rubber stair nosings at both existing stairs. The existing concrete stair edges are worn and chipped up to 3/4 inch, and the rubber nosings will not bear on them. Please advise.
Use aluminum abrasive nosings anchored into the concrete, with epoxy fill at the chipped edges.
Change the nosings at both existing stairs to aluminum abrasive nosings anchored into the concrete, with epoxy fill at the chipped edges, as suggested.

documents.title: RFI-158 Bleacher anchors at existing gym slab

pieces.body: Drawing S-310 shows wedge anchors for the telescoping bleachers. Cores taken in the existing gym slab tested at 2,500 psi, below the 4,000 psi assumed for the wedge anchor capacity. Please advise.
Use adhesive (epoxy) anchors at the same spacing.
Use epoxy adhesive anchors, 5/8 inch diameter with 5 inch embedment, at the spacing shown on S-310. Special inspection is required.

documents.title: RFI-162 Vapor retarder under addition slab

pieces.body: Detail 1/S-101 shows a vapor retarder under the addition slab on grade but no thickness. Please confirm.
Use a 15-mil vapor retarder with taped seams.
Use a 15-mil vapor retarder meeting ASTM E1745 Class A, seams taped, as suggested. Answered in the general structural notes.
Drawing M-501 shows the new rooftop units RTU-3 and RTU-4 set on the existing curbs. The scheduled units have a larger footprint than the existing curbs. Please advise.
Provide manufactured curb adapters for RTU-3 and RTU-4.
Provide manufactured curb adapters for RTU-3 and RTU-4. See ASI-034 for the revised detail on M-501.

documents.title: RFI-171 Classroom fire alarm notification devices

pieces.body: Drawing FA-101 shows horn-only notification devices in the classrooms. Classrooms are occupied spaces and require visible notification. Please confirm the device type.
Replace classroom horns with horn/strobes, 75 cd minimum.
Provide horn/strobe devices in all classrooms in place of the horns shown on FA-101.

documents.title: RFI-175 Closers at corridor doors C201 to C212

pieces.body: Please confirm whether closers are required at corridor doors C201 to C212.
Provide surface closers at C201 to C212.
Closers are required per HW-4.
Drawing M-401 shows the kitchen exhaust hood on the east wall. The existing roof beam at that wall blocks the duct riser to the roof. Please advise.
Relocate the hood to the south wall, where the riser can pass between beams.
Relocate the kitchen hood to the south wall as suggested. Revised layout on sketch SK-180 attached.

documents.title: RFI-183 Gas shutoff at science rooms

pieces.body: Drawing P-220 shows gas outlets at the lab benches in science rooms 201 and 203 but no room shutoff. The fire code requires an emergency shutoff for each lab room. Please advise.
Add a solenoid emergency gas shutoff valve with a push-button station at the door of each room.
Provide a solenoid emergency gas shutoff valve with a push-button station at the exit door of rooms 201 and 203, as suggested.
The elevator pit on A-130 shows a sump but no pump or oil interceptor. Please confirm.
Provide a sump with a duplex pump; no oil interceptor (machine-roomless traction elevator).
Provide the sump with a single submersible pump discharging to the storm system. An oil interceptor is not required for the traction elevator.

documents.title: RFI-196 Hardware finish at gym doors

pieces.body: Gym door hardware sets do not state a finish. Please confirm.
Use satin chrome, 626.
Use satin chrome, BHMA 626, per Section 08 71 00 paragraph 2.01.A. Answered in the Contract Documents.

documents.title: RFI-205 Wing A casework and new data outlets

pieces.body: Drawing A-401 places casework on the corridor walls of rooms 110 to 118, where T-101 shows the new data outlets and the MEP rough-in - Wing A is already routed. Please advise.
Move the casework to the exterior walls of each room.
Move the casework to the opposite (exterior) walls of rooms 110 to 118. See ASI-061.

documents.title: RFI-214 Gym roof truss bearing at existing masonry wall

pieces.body: Detail 4/S-301 shows a standard bearing plate for the gym roof trusses at the existing masonry wall. The plate holes conflict with the existing wall's anchor layout found in the field. How should the trusses bear?
Provide slotted bearing assemblies, field-welded after the trusses are set.

documents.title: CP-0404 Added play structure at primary playground

pieces.body: Added play structure at primary playground. Owner added a second play structure and its safety surfacing at the primary playground. Scope basis: Drawing L-201 shows one play structure.
Owner direction: Owner email 2020-06-17, event date 2020-06-17. Notice given 2020-06-20; CP submitted 2020-07-04.
Total requested $125,809.60: subcontractor quotes $77,352.00; extended SGC for time $44,590.00; Fee at 5% $3,867.60.

14 calendar days requested. The new structure is installed after the playground and play surfacing work and must be finished before final striping and site cleanup. New activity F-0404A, Install added play structure and surfacing, takes 10 working days. F-0404A cannot start until A2140 (Playground and play surfacing) finishes. A2170 (Striping and final site cleanup) cannot start until F-0404A finishes. CM requests 14 calendar days of time extension and extended general conditions for those days.

documents.title: CP-0405 Revised casework blocking per ASI-061

pieces.body: Revised casework blocking per ASI-061. ASI-061 moves the Wing A classroom casework to the opposite walls. Framing sub adds blocking and patches the moved locations. Scope basis: Drawing A-401 shows casework on the corridor walls of rooms 110 to 118.
ASI: ASI-061, event date 2020-06-19. Notice given 2020-06-23; CP submitted 2020-07-06.
Total requested $53,001.69: subcontractor quotes $14,077.80; extended SGC for time $38,220.00; Fee at 5% $703.89.

12 calendar days requested. The blocking work follows the Wing A framing and drywall and has to be done before painting in the existing building starts. New activity F-0405A, Rework casework blocking - Wing A (ASI-061), takes 8 working days. F-0405A cannot start until A1700 (Framing and drywall - Wing A) finishes. A1750 (Painting - existing building) cannot start until F-0405A finishes. CM requests 12 calendar days of time extension and extended general conditions for those days.

documents.title: CP-0406 PV-ready roof upgrade at addition

pieces.body: PV-ready roof upgrade at addition. Owner directed a PV-ready roof at the addition: added blocking, conduit sleeves and thicker insulation under the membrane. Scope basis: Spec 07 54 23 covers a standard TPO roof with R-30 insulation and no solar provisions.
Owner direction: Owner letter 2020-06-22, event date 2020-06-22. Notice given 2020-06-25; CP submitted 2020-07-09.
Total requested $111,998.95: subcontractor quotes $55,099.00; extended SGC for time $54,145.00; Fee at 5% $2,754.95.

17 calendar days requested. The added blocking and insulation work starts after the metal deck and elevated slab are complete, and the roofing membrane cannot start until it is done. CM's claim counts the whole 12 working days of added work. New activity F-0406A, PV-ready blocking and added roof insulation - addition, takes 12 working days. F-0406A cannot start until A1470 (Metal deck and elevated slab - addition) finishes. A1520 (Roofing - addition) cannot start until F-0406A finishes. CM requests 17 calendar days of time extension and extended general conditions for those days.

documents.title: CP-0407 Storefront head subframing per RFI-233

pieces.body: Storefront head subframing per RFI-233. RFI-233 response revises the storefront head detail at the addition and adds steel subframing above every storefront opening. Scope basis: Drawing A-501 detail 7 shows storefront heads anchored directly to the framing.
RFI response: RFI-233, event date 2020-06-24. Notice given 2020-06-29; CP submitted 2020-07-13.
Total requested $79,474.50: subcontractor quotes $11,990.00; extended SGC for time $66,885.00; Fee at 5% $599.50.

21 calendar days requested. The subframing goes in after the exterior framing and sheathing at the addition and must be in place before windows and storefront can be set. New activity F-0407A, Install storefront head subframing (RFI-233), takes 4 working days. F-0407A cannot start until A1510 (Exterior framing and sheathing - addition) finishes. A1530 (Windows and storefront - addition) cannot start until F-0407A finishes. CM requests 21 calendar days of time extension and extended general conditions for those days.

documents.title: CP-0408 Rerouted sprinkler mains per ASI-070

pieces.body: Rerouted sprinkler mains per ASI-070. ASI-070 reroutes the addition's sprinkler mains around the revised duct mains and adds two zones. Scope basis: Drawing FP-201 shows the mains running through the corridor ceiling space.
ASI: ASI-070, event date 2020-06-25. Notice given 2020-06-29; CP submitted 2020-07-13.
Total requested $78,856.54: subcontractor quotes $32,634.80; extended SGC for time $44,590.00; Fee at 5% $1,631.74.

New activity F-0408A, Reroute sprinkler mains - addition (ASI-070), takes 9 working days. F-0408A cannot start until A1640 (Fire sprinkler rough-in - addition) finishes. A1685 (In-wall and above-ceiling inspections - addition) cannot start until F-0408A finishes. CM requests 14 calendar days of time extension and extended general conditions for those days.

documents.title: CP-0409 Steel erection start: erector crane availability

pieces.body: Steel erection start: erector crane availability. The steel erector advised that its crawler crane is committed to another job and will arrive 5 working days later than planned. CM asks for time and the erector's standby cost. Scope basis: Subcontract with the erector requires mobilization within 3 days of notice.
Other event: Erector letter 2020-06-10, event date 2020-06-10. Notice given 2020-06-16; CP submitted 2020-06-30.

New activity F-0409A, Wait for erector's crane (erector's commitment elsewhere), takes 5 working days. F-0409A cannot start until A1430 (Slab on grade - addition) finishes. A1460 (Erect structural steel - addition) cannot start until F-0409A finishes. CM requests 7 calendar days of time extension, time only.

documents.title: CP-0410 Flatwork crew shortage at site

pieces.body: Flatwork crew shortage at site. The flatwork sub reports a crew shortage and will start curbs and sidewalks 8 working days late. CM asks for time only. Scope basis: Subcontract schedule requires flatwork to follow site electrical directly.
Other event: Sub letter 2020-06-15, event date 2020-06-15. Notice given 2020-06-20; CP submitted 2020-07-04.
Total requested $0.00.

New activity F-0410A, Flatwork crew unavailable (subcontractor shortage), takes 8 working days. F-0410A cannot start until A2110 (Site electrical and lighting conduit) finishes. A2130 (Curbs, sidewalks and flatwork) cannot start until F-0410A finishes. CM requests 10 calendar days of time extension, time only.

documents.title: CP-0411 Abnormal rainfall at addition excavation

pieces.body: Abnormal rainfall at addition excavation. Rainfall in early June 2020 was well above the ten-year average at the nearest NOAA station and flooded the addition footprint. CM pumped the site and asks for time only. Scope basis: Daily reports and NOAA data attached.
Other event: Daily reports 2020-06-03 to 2020-06-08, event date 2020-06-03. Notice given 2020-06-10; CP submitted 2020-06-24.
Total requested $1,779.62: CM direct costs $1,694.88; Fee at 5% $84.74.

New activity F-0411A, Weather standby - abnormal rainfall at addition footprint, takes 4 working days. F-0411A cannot start until A1340 (Haul-off and clear addition footprint) finishes. A1400 (Excavation and shoring - addition) cannot start until F-0411A finishes. CM requests 7 calendar days of time extension, time only.

Flooded underslab utility trench. A second abnormal storm flooded the open underslab utility trench at the addition. The trench has to be dewatered, re-excavated and the bedding replaced. CM asks for time only. Scope basis: Daily reports and NOAA data attached.
Other event: Daily reports 2020-06-26 to 2020-06-30, event date 2020-06-26. Notice given 2020-07-02; CP submitted 2020-07-16.
Total requested $4,431.84: CM direct costs $4,220.80; Fee at 5% $211.04.

New activity F-0412A, Dewater and re-excavate flooded underslab utility trench, takes 15 working days. F-0412A cannot start until A1410 (Underslab utilities - addition) finishes. A1430 (Slab on grade - addition) cannot start until F-0412A finishes. CM requests 21 calendar days of time extension, time only.

documents.title: CP-0413 Classroom flooring change (concurrent with crew shortage)

pieces.body: Classroom flooring change (concurrent with crew shortage). Owner changed the addition classroom flooring from VCT to rubber tile, which adds a resubmittal and longer lead time. Separately, the flooring sub has told CM it will be short a crew for the same period. Scope basis: Spec 09 65 19 specifies VCT in classrooms 201 to 212.
Owner direction: Owner email 2020-06-29, event date 2020-06-29. Notice given 2020-07-02; CP submitted 2020-07-16.
Total requested $76,328.56: subcontractor quotes $39,327.20; extended SGC for time $35,035.00; Fee at 5% $1,966.36.

11 calendar days requested. Both delays fall between the addition ceilings and the addition classroom flooring. The Owner's change adds 6 working days for the resubmittal and delivery; the sub's crew shortage would by itself also hold the flooring start by 6 working days, over the same period. New activity F-0413A, Resubmit and deliver rubber flooring (Owner change), takes 6 working days. New activity F-0413B, Flooring crew shortage (subcontractor), takes 6 working days. F-0413A cannot start until A1740 (Ceilings - addition) finishes. A1790 (Flooring - addition classrooms) cannot start until F-0413A finishes. F-0413B cannot start until A1740 (Ceilings - addition) finishes. A1790 (Flooring - addition classrooms) cannot start until F-0413B finishes. CM requests 11 calendar days of time extension and extended general conditions for those days.

documents.title: CP-0414 Sunshades at existing windows per ASI-075

ASI: ASI-075, event date 2020-06-30. Notice given 2020-07-04; CP submitted 2020-07-18.
Total requested $36,692.04: subcontractor quotes $34,944.80; Fee at 5% $1,747.24.

No time requested. The sunshades are installed after the existing-building window replacement and before exterior painting and sealants. CM requests no time. New activity F-0414A, Install sunshades - existing building (ASI-075), takes 6 working days. F-0414A cannot start until A1560 (Window replacement - existing building) finishes. A1580 (Exterior painting and sealants - existing building) cannot start until F-0414A finishes. CM requests no extension of time.

documents.title: CP-0415 Added data drops in Wing B offices
